items.what_happened: At 12:21 its list queued the next step (#as10) behind the frame at 60%. At 12:26 armadvsol_6103, another builder's frame 229 elmos away, finished. The finish handler matches a builder's started build by type within 250 elmos, so it took that as 15311's build finishing and promoted the queued #as10 order to the task (started=false). The builder was still building 19432 (71% at 12:30, 86% at 12:45). From 12:41 it stood 218 from #as10's placed site (1808,7024), inside reach+margin 250. The blocked-site watchdog only looks for a same-type frame within 200 of that site, and 19432 is 215 away, so it missed it. After 8 s the watchdog stopped the builder with the frame at 86%. It peaked at 92% and decayed from 12:51. The list re-sent #as10 elsewhere (started 13:25 at 2512,7312).

mechanisms: The finish handler matches a builder's started build by type within 250 elmos, and the blocked-site watchdog checks the builder's own frame only within 200 of the queued order's site. A neighbour's frame of the same type finishing nearby promoted constructor_15311's queued order while its own frame stood at 71%, and the watchdog then stopped it at 86% (armadvsol_19432, 322 metal). Keying the task to the frame's unit id and skipping builders with a frame of their own in progress would have kept the 322. The same match emptied 15311's task at 15:56 and 3778's at 16:20 without loss.

The player's own `stop` on started frames dropped 247 metal: armnanotc_372 (159) and armvp_22187 (88). The nano was at 54% in the report and 69% when the stop landed; it was dropped to clear an exit lane that the report said its constructor stood in, not the frame. The plant was at 1% in the report and 15% at landing, and the same call withdrew its helper. A queue result or entry giving the share at landing and the seconds to finish, or moving only the builder to clear a lane, would have kept them.

No third mechanism lost frame metal. The report's abandoned line gives the share at destruction ('(0% built)' for all three, 569 metal), so the player was never told what it lost; that line recovers nothing by itself. The costliest never-started pattern was the list's 'taken as done' on an order not yet begun (6:57, 7:19, 15:08; fixed after this game in e9f5175). It cost no frame metal, but spot_87 stood without an extractor or turret from 7:30 to 11:00 and spot_91 never got its moho.
unread: Nothing torn. floor.py's aband 3 equals the decayed count; its aband_m reads 6 against frames.py's 569 because it takes each frame's last sampled share before destruction (near 0 after a decay), while frames.py takes the peak. hands_window was run only around the U9 item (no plan play for 15311), since no U1 item needed it.
